How this lesson works

This activity is adapted directly from the worksheet you uploaded — a listening exercise called Cocktail international, recorded for the European Day of Languages. Here is the original task, translated:

Original instructions (French → English)
“Regardez ci-dessus la liste des participants au cocktail. Puis observez les dessins et écoutez les dialogues.”
Look at the guest list below. Then look at the four drawings and listen to the dialogues.
  1. Find each person on the guest list.
  2. Match each dialogue you hear to the drawing it belongs to.

Use the audio bar at the top of the page — it stays visible as you scroll. You can play the whole recording, or use the Dialogue 1–4 buttons to jump to each conversation (the four are separated by pauses on the original recording).

02

Vocabulary — nationality adjectives

Every guest on the list is described by a nationality adjective. In French, these adjectives agree with gender — the form changes depending on whether you're describing a man or a woman.

GuestNationality (as listed)English
Pattern
  • Most adjectives: add -e for the feminine — allemand → allemande, américain → américaine
  • Ending in -ien: → -ienne — canadien → canadienne, coréen → coréenne
  • Ending in -is/-ois: add -e — français → française, suédois → suédoise
  • Ending in -c: → -que — grec → grecque
  • Ending in -ol: → -ole — espagnol → espagnole
  • Already ending in -e: no change — russe → russe

Quick practice — give the feminine form

Type the feminine form of each masculine nationality. Accents matter for the "correct" mark, but a close answer still gets useful feedback.

04

Now you try — introduce two guests

Pick two people from the guest list and write a short introduction dialogue between them, the way the guests at the cocktail party do. Click a phrase to add it to your draft.

Model dialogue — Bonjour, je m'appelle Karl. Et vous ?
— Je m'appelle Alexandra. Vous êtes allemand ?
— Oui, je suis allemand, de Berlin. Et vous, quelle est votre nationalité ?
— Je suis grecque, d'Athènes. Enchantée, Karl !
— Enchanté, Alexandra !
